parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the magnification produced by a converging lens. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Measure and record the height h O of the illuminated object. h O = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Place the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated object. Place the screen near the lens and switch on the lamp. Move the screen until a clear focused image of the illuminated object is seen. Measure, and record in Table 3.1, the height h I of the image. Repeat the procedure for u = 25.0 cm, 30.0 cm, 35.0 cm and 40.0 cm. Switch off the lamp. Table 3.1 u / cm h I / cm W 20.0 25.0 30.0 35.0 40.0 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) For each distance u , calculate, and record in Table 3.1, a value W using your results from (a) and the equation W = h O h I . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of u / cm ( y -axis) against W ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:
axes labelled correct orientation, with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to less than ½ small square and precise plots
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The gradient of the line on the graph is numerically equal to the focal length f of the lens. Calculate a value of f for this experiment. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information to determine the gradient. f = ........................................................ [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
triangle method seen on graph
f in range 12 (cm) to 18 (cm)

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
